author: hsnabdulla
quote:
This game doesn't just follow the series' legacy; it redefines it by perfectly balancing psychological dread with high-stakes tactical combat.​ Here is why this game stands out as a pinnacle of the genre:​
Grace's Gameplay: The Essence of True Horror
​Grace’s segments are a masterclass in True Horror. While many modern games lean too heavily on action, Grace’s gameplay forces you back into a state of vulnerability. Every creak of a floorboard and every flickering light feels like a genuine threat. Because she isn't a powerhouse, you have to rely on stealth, resource management, and pure survival instinct. It creates a suffocating atmosphere of dread that reminds us why we fell in love with Resident Evil in the first place—the fear of the unknown and the constant feeling of being hunted.​
Leon's Gameplay: A Combat Specialist at Work
​On the flip side, playing as Leon Kennedy is a completely different, yet equally satisfying experience. It perfectly showcases just how knowledgeable and seasoned he is in fighting. Leon isn’t just a guy with a gun anymore; he is a veteran of biological warfare. His movements are precise, his CQC (Close Quarters Combat) is fluid, and his tactical awareness is top-tier. You can feel his years of experience in every parry and every calculated shot. It’s the perfect representation of a survivor who has evolved into a professional protector.​
The contrast between Grace’s raw, terrifying struggle and Leon’s tactical expertise makes Resident Evil Requiem an absolute triumph. It gives you the best of both worlds: the adrenaline of the fight and the cold chill of the shadows.
